supersedesNothing: tests/preflight-false-positive-measurement-2026-10-07.json is preserved unchanged as the pre-fix measurement. Version 1 of this file recorded a fix that an independent review then falsified; version 2 records the repaired state and the review outcome.
method: read-only offline run of the exported guards over every retained incremental-learning dossier under ~/.cache/pi-continual-learning/docker. No model, service or network call. Only counts, masked shapes and synthetic fixtures are stored.

firstFix.change: documentation-style placeholder values are not credentials; a realistic assigned value stays sensitive
firstFix.regression: tests/test_jev_learning.py covers `passwd: <password>` (allowed) beside `password = hunter2long`, a provider key and an AWS access key (refused)

secondDefectFound.detector: sensitiveValue (Jev preflight in extensions/jev-learning.ts), a separate detector from the Memory guard
secondDefectFound.cause: its JSON-quoted credential regex had no placeholder rule, and the Memory guard's assignment pattern did not match a quoted key at all, so the same text could be refused by the preflight and allowed by the Memory guard

reviewRoundTrip.review: An independent reviewer with no implementation history falsified two claims of version 1 before any paid call; every finding was repaired.
reviewRoundTrip.falsifiedFinding1: Removing the preflight's inline quoted-assignment regex lost coverage for a quoted value whose text contains a comma, semicolon, question mark or `//`, because the shared pattern's value class stops at `,`/`;` and the string did not parse as JSON. Reproduced: sensitiveValue('Config: {"password": "My,Secret1"}') was true before and false after.
reviewRoundTrip.falsifiedFinding2: Applying the documentation-placeholder rule to the credential-named structured-key rule exonerated realistic values, including a value containing `?` or `&&` and a `sample`/`test`-prefixed value.
reviewRoundTrip.repair1: Added QUOTED_ASSIGNED_CREDENTIAL_PATTERN with a quote-bounded value class and routed it through the same placeholder rule, so a quoted assignment is always matched and then judged, whatever punctuation it contains.
reviewRoundTrip.repair2: Tightened CODE_OR_ENV_PATTERN so its expression clause requires whitespace around `?`, `||`, `&&` or `+`, and reverted the placeholder rule on the credential-named structured-key rule: text placeholders stay exempt, object keys stay strict. Failing closed here can only refuse more, never less.
reviewRoundTrip.repair3: scripts/validate-consolidate.py now mirrors the quoted pattern and the placeholder rule; the shared corpus pins both implementations.
reviewRoundTrip.repair4: Corrected the invariant and boundary text in this file, the changeset and CONTEXT.md, and replaced the unreproducible suite claim with a re-run command and count.

reviewRoundTrip2.review: A second independent re-review falsified claims 1, 2 (as worded) and 5 again before any paid call, and required four repairs.
reviewRoundTrip2.falsified1: The delimited pattern required a quoted key and its value class rejected both quote characters, so a quoted value under an unquoted key, or a value containing the other quote type or an escaped quote, was allowed by both detectors.
reviewRoundTrip2.falsified2: The Memory guard's parsed-object member path still applied the placeholder rule, so it allowed {"apiKey": "sampledata99"} while the preflight refused the equivalent argument: the two detectors disagreed about one record.
reviewRoundTrip2.falsified4: scripts/validate-consolidate.py never received the optional-quote key class, so the packed validator allowed 1400 of 14444 probes the runtime refuses.
reviewRoundTrip2.repair1: The delimited pattern now accepts either key form and both quote types with backslash escapes, and excludes only a real URL scheme; the plain pattern's credential-key class accepts optional surrounding quotes.
reviewRoundTrip2.repair2: credentialNamedKeyAssignsValue is exported and used by both detectors, so a credential-named structured member or object key is strict everywhere.
reviewRoundTrip2.repair3: The Python validator mirrors both patterns, and its comment now states that the runtime can refuse more for JSON-looking text.
reviewRoundTrip2.repair4: Corpus entries for the delimiter shapes were added and the artifact wording was corrected, including the fact that the credential-key class was widened for detection only.

reviewRoundTrip3.review: A third independent review falsified requirement 3 and requirement 6 before any paid call: the pre-change preflight refused realistic secrets that the current one allowed, and the URL exclusion differed between the text path and the structured path.
reviewRoundTrip3.falsified3: The pre-change preflight's inline quoted-assignment regex had no URL exclusion, so it refused {"password": "://Xq7bN2mP4kL9vR3s"}, {"password": "mongodb+srv://user:Xq7bN2mP4kL9vR3s@h/db"} and {"password": "Xq7bN2mP4kL9vR3s://x"}. The current delimited pattern excluded anything scheme-shaped, and the structured-key predicate excluded any value containing `://`, so all three were allowed.
reviewRoundTrip3.falsified6: The text path used a scheme-shaped URL exclusion while the structured path used a bare `includes("://")`, so the same secret was refused as text and allowed as a parsed member, and any secret could be hidden behind a fake scheme prefix.
reviewRoundTrip3.falsified5: The artifact said the corpus gained eleven sensitive entries (twelve at the time) and CONTEXT.md still said no pattern class was widened.
reviewRoundTrip3.repair: One shared URL rule now serves both detectors and the packed validator: a value is exempted as a URL only when it starts with a well-known scheme (http, https, ftp, ftps, ssh, git, git+ssh, svn, ws, wss, file) and carries no userinfo. The regex lookaheads were removed from both patterns so the rule is applied in one place. The artifact counts and the widening wording were corrected.

reviewRoundTrip4.review: A fourth independent review (after a provider-timeout retry) falsified requirement 3 again and required one more repair.
reviewRoundTrip4.falsified: The URL exemption itself was the smuggling channel. All three implementations allowed credential-bearing URL values that the pre-change preflight refused, for example {"password": "https://hooks.slack.com/services/T00000000/B00000000/XXXX"}, {"password": "https://Xq7bN2mP4kL9vR3s@host"} and {"password": "https://Xq7bN2mP4kL9vR3s"}. Every scheme list and userinfo test was bypassed in review.
reviewRoundTrip4.repair: The URL exemption was removed for credential-named assignments in all three implementations. The documented placeholder rule is the only exemption, and it still covers code, env and expression references. A credential-named key whose value is a plain URL is now refused: that is the fail-closed direction and a deliberate false-positive cost, because no shape test can separate a token-bearing URL from an ordinary one.
reviewRoundTrip4.artifactFix: Corpus entries for credential-named URL values moved from benign to sensitive, the invariant text was corrected, and the round-2 repair note below is superseded: the URL exemption described there was removed in round 4.

reviewRoundTrip5.review: A fifth independent review found no behavioral contradiction and no bypass of the current rules. It reported only stale comments left by superseded rounds.
reviewRoundTrip5.finding: Stale comments still described a URL exemption in extensions/consolidation-run.ts, scripts/validate-consolidate.py, CONTEXT.md and this artifact's round-2 note. Two bounded smuggles it found in prose text (a parenthesised value and a sample-prefixed value) are the pre-existing documented placeholder rule, are allowed by the pre-change code too, and are refused on the structured-key path.
reviewRoundTrip5.repair: The stale comments were corrected to state that a credential-named assignment has no URL exemption and that the placeholder rule is the only exemption.
reviewRoundTrip5.verdict: PAID RUN: MAY PROCEED - no regression versus the pre-change preflight and no remaining behavioral claim contradicted.

changes: QUOTED_ASSIGNED_CREDENTIAL_PATTERN matches a quoted credential assignment with a punctuation-tolerant value and is judged by placeholderCredentialValue
CODE_OR_ENV_PATTERN requires whitespace around an expression operator, so a password containing `?` or `&&` is not read as an expression
the Jev preflight no longer applies the placeholder rule to a credential-named structured object key
scripts/validate-consolidate.py mirrors both patterns and the placeholder rule
the delimited pattern accepts either key form and both quote types with escapes, and the credential-key class accepts optional surrounding quotes (detection widening only)
the URL exemption was removed: a credential-named key with an assigned value is refused, URL or not, and only the documented placeholder rule exempts
fix.invariant: No placeholder allowlist entry was added and no secret value class was loosened. A credential-named assignment has no URL exemption in any of the three implementations, so a scheme-less value, an unknown scheme, a userinfo-bearing value, a webhook URL and an ordinary URL under such a key are all refused. The only widening is the plain pattern's credential-key class accepting optional surrounding quotes, which widens detection and never sensitivity, because every matched assignment still passes through the placeholder rule. A credential-named structured member or object key is strict in both detectors.

sampleLimit: Zero trips over 169 dossiers and 4677 entries does not give a false-positive rate, and it cannot prove that no other placeholder shape trips either detector. The retained dossiers are one public-project corpus. No live cohort was re-run for this verification.
boundary: This proves the two detectors and the packed validator judge a documented text placeholder identically and refuse every tested realistic value, including URL-shaped and scheme-less credentials, at the cost of also refusing an ordinary URL that appears under a credential-named key. It does not establish a false-positive rate, does not cover every placeholder shape, and does not replace the paid cohort.
